checks_run.procedure: D-225 open question 1: look for a column, response or write path that references a sensitive record and that the inventory does not classify or classifies wrongly. The catalog test enumerates only fk, uuid, uuid[] and json columns, so text columns and responses outside each row's operation list were probed on the real API: inbox notifications (list and mark-read) about a Finance validation (producer shape), a benefit overlap (real POST /benefit-overlaps producer) and a benefit route; plus a scan of every text/varchar column for the hidden ids.
checks_run.environment: Clone w2 (unbuilt, probe only), Node 22.22.0, LANG unset, disposable PostgreSQL, demo seed
checks_run.expected: No response names a hidden id or the restricted record's code to a recipient who gets 404 on it.
checks_run.actual: Exit 1 by design: 3 of 5 tests fail, each because it found a leak. 'P1 work item ... inbox list and mark-read' fails with 3 leaks: listMyInbox and markInboxNotificationRead return the Finance validation notification unredacted (benefitCode B01, period, the fv id in linkPath) while the same user's work item is redacted. 'P1b benefit overlap (real producer)' fails with 2 leaks: the Finance recipient (404 on the benefit and the overlap) sees benefitACode B04 and the overlap id in linkPath. 'P1c mark-read' fails: the list shows inbox.restricted but keeps linkPath with the hidden benefit id, and POST /me/inbox/{id}/read returns {benefitCode: B01}. The 2 passing tests are the 404 control and the text scan (1702 text/varchar columns; the hidden ids occur only in finance_validation.idempotency_key, inbox_notification.dedupe_key and .link_path, work_item.dedupe_key and .link_path; the dedupe and idempotency keys are not serialized, work_item.link_path is redacted by BE-Z12B, inbox_notification.link_path is not). Raised as F-DG6-540 (Medium). The probe file came from the interrupted earlier attempt of my role; I read it in full and ran it in this run.

checks_run.procedure: Challenge the D-222 (2) re-save rule for automation conditions: a not-admitted author removes an earlier condition with the same field and operator (the editor's 'remove condition' button) and saves the remaining conditions, marker included, unchanged.
checks_run.environment: Clone w2, Node 22.22.0, LANG unset, disposable PostgreSQL, in-tree BE-Z12B fixtures
checks_run.expected: The hidden literal is kept, or the write is refused; the marker text is never stored in its place.
checks_run.actual: Exit 1 by design: the single test fails on 'expected [...] not to contain "[restricted]"'. The PATCH answers 200 with no marker; the stored conditions become [benefitId neq "[restricted]", severity eq high]; the sensitive benefit's id is gone from the version, so the rule no longer excludes it; the admitted TO sees the literal "[restricted]". Raised as F-DG6-541 (Medium).

checks_run.procedure: Judge the D-223 write-side trade-off (free-text condition literals and procedure subjects are not existence-checked, so a writer who types a hidden id later sees the marker).
checks_run.environment: Source reading of automation/versions.ts, procedures/instances.ts and access/sensitive-reach.ts; the round-7 reproduction's audit read (log 41)
checks_run.expected: The marker discloses nothing the writer could not already know.
checks_run.actual: Accepted, not a defect. The marker appears only if the writer already holds the exact id (UUIDv7: 74 random bits, not guessable), and an in-scope reader can already obtain hidden record ids from the transformation audit trail, which D-219 excuses: log 41 shows TL's unfiltered audit list names the hidden benefit as a recordId. So the write-side marker gives no new existence oracle. Refusing such literals would add a 422 on a free-text field with no gain. The separate re-save defect is F-DG6-541.

checks_run.procedure: Read the whole diff 70f05ed4..d84d11a6 (63 files: product, contract, ADR, data dictionary, ERD) and the files it touches; check each changed mutation for authorization re-checked in the transaction, validation, If-Match, one audit event and no remote I/O in the transaction.
checks_run.expected: No new authorization, integrity or injection defect beyond those raised.
checks_run.actual: benefits/register.ts: presentBenefits hides parentBenefitId and businessCaseLineId; checkBenefitRules refuses a hidden parent (unknownReference) and a hidden case line before the 'taken' 409, so no oracle; the re-save keeps a hidden ref only when null is sent, and a new id still replaces it. launch/tasks.ts: read hidden; write refused as unknown; re-save keeps; createTask accepts no output. meeting-outputs.ts, procedures/steps.ts, workflows/approvals.ts, raid/actions.ts, sustainment/controls.ts, revision-impact.ts, reporting/orphans.ts and my-work.ts present through the reach helpers. The My Work cursor uses the work-item id for a restricted item, so the cursor names no hidden id. The tasks/routes.ts COMPLETE response is now redacted. No mutation lost its If-Match, its audit event or its in-transaction session re-check; every changed write keeps the existing locks and audit calls, and no remote I/O was added. One observation, not a defect: revision-impact.ts redacts proposals with one await per row (bounded by the page limit). The automation re-save (F-DG6-541) and the inbox (F-DG6-540) are the defects found. ARCH-16's ADR, OpenAPI and data-dictionary text matches the code I read, except that it inherits the inbox inventory classification F-DG6-540 shows is wrong.

summary: FAIL. F-DG6-480 is CLOSED_VERIFIED: the round-7 reproduction passes unchanged (no leak; the write oracle is now 422/422), the in-tree tests pass, and all four mutants are caught. All required checks ran and pass, with two disclosed environmental re-runs: build, static checks, 932 operations, unit tests on Node 24 and 22 (a Vitest worker RPC timeout under load forced a re-run), integration in both locales (4298 tests each; 932/932 responses validated; migrations 0001-0126), and historical DG1-DG5. Two new Medium findings. F-DG6-540: the inbox still names sensitive records to recipients who get 404 on them. The list keeps the hidden id in linkPath, mark-read returns the unredacted text, and Finance-validation and benefit-overlap notifications show the sensitive benefit's code. The BE-Z12 inventory misses this because link_path is a text column and markInboxNotificationRead is not in its operation list. F-DG6-541: removing an earlier rule condition in the editor silently replaces a hidden condition literal with the text "[restricted]", so the rule stops excluding the sensitive benefit. The D-223 write-side trade-off is accepted.
